newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria cabinet approves 1997 draft budget frame.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria cabinet approves 1997 draft budget frame.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet on Thursday approved the 1997 draft budget frame as part of preparations to launch a currency board on July 1, government officials said.
"The cabinet approved in principle the draft budget and will discuss the budget item by item on Friday," Finance Minister Muravei Radev told reporters.
The draft budget frame agreed with the IMF last week envisages revenue at 27.3 percent of GDP and expenditure at 33.5 percent of GDP.

The budget deficit was assumed at 6.2 percent of GDP, higher than IMF-recommended 3.8 percent due to pending interest payments on Bulgarian foreign and domestic debt, but lower than last year's 13 percent said Radev. Assumed GDP is 16.15 trillion levs.
Prime Minister Kostov said the budget bill will be introduced to parliamentary committees for debate on Monday aiming to pass it in plenary session by end of June.
"A budget that envisages the introduction of a currency board can hardly please anyone," said Kostov.

Under the IMF-prescribed currency board system, central bank lending to the government and commercial banks is banned and levs in circulation must be fully covered by foreign exchange reserves at a fixed rate of 1,000 levs to the mark.
"We will mobilise all our efforts to collect the revenue set in the budget including the tax and customs authorities," said Kostov.
The government plans to fund most of the deficit by proceeds from privatisation and taxes.
